# Saved building-block objects

Original fixture generated by `tools/docpart_object_fixture.py` from the
repository's minimal original OPC skeleton. No corpus document or artwork is
included. Four controls cover block and inline contents, empty properties,
gallery/category metadata, and absent/false/zero boolean values.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.11, 17.5.2.13 and 17.5.2.14 describe gallery,
document-part object and built-in-document-part identification. Saved contents
need not match an installed gallery entry. `docPartUnique` is not a constraint
on the number of object instances.

The reference application renders one page. `native.pdf` was exported read-only
with `tools/export-reference.ps1`, including explicit repagination. The
native/browser full-page pair was visually inspected. Source SHA-256:
`af211e9c067f239cff6caa4fa672b03ae147566d412d7a0c2a38328dcd190821`.
PDF SHA-256:
`b68666d23850ae36bb0dfc60349cd24372a3be20274a33c5b85276829c6a76cc`.

`tools/record_docpart_object.ps1 -SkipPdf` records native edits to Alpha, Beta,
Gamma and Delta. `native-edited.xml` is the reference application's in-memory Flat OPC export after
those edits; it is not a saved DOCX. `native-edit-reference.json` binds source and
XML hashes. The reference application's ContentControls collection reports zero, but the actual XML
retains all four `w:sdt` wrappers and the four edited strings.

The reference application normalizes metadata: the first object becomes gallery/unique/category,
contrary to the schema's gallery/category/unique sequence; empty and
category-only block metadata acquire AutoText defaults; the inline object's
docPartObj property is removed while its wrapper survives. The importer accepts
unique known properties in any order and preserves source metadata instead of
applying the reference application's destructive normalization. Tests bind the native evidence and
exercise its observed ordering in an independently constructed package.

The editor renders and edits saved content; it does not offer a gallery picker.
No-edit and undo preserve every package part. Edited exports retain control
properties and unrelated parts, and reopen editable. Unknown/duplicate
properties, invalid values and conflicting content types reject safely.
